books.blurb: One bond yield quietly sets your home loan.

books.title: The Debt Loop
books.blurb: Why borrowing to pay interest feeds itself.
gist: The US owes about $40 trillion and now pays over $1 trillion a year in interest, much of it with new borrowing.
Every new IOU travels through money plumbing: reserves, repo and money funds. Tight pipes make borrowing pricier.
Leveraged bets on Treasuries work until margin calls hit, and new money reaches asset owners before wage earners.

books.title: Two Schools of Economics
books.blurb: One recession, two readings of what went wrong.
gist: Keynesians focus on the slump: when spending falls, government or the central bank steps in to lift it, and leans against overheating.
Austrians focus on the boom: cheap credit pushes firms to build things people won't end up wanting, and the bust is the cleanup.
On money, Keynesians see the central bank as a tool to steady the economy; Austrians say its money creation sends false signals.
